text:
alex: Oof, need a quick sweep and brainshare — microbatch size tuning for streaming chat vs non-streaming (bulk) completions. Goal: streaming tail p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 700ms if possible, otherwise quantify throughput tradeoffs. Can we capture kernel selection events + KV-cache hit rates per config?

maya: On it. I'll run mb=4/8/16 for streaming and bulk, collect kernel logs + kv stats. Will post short summary.

perf-bot: Job scheduled: mb-sweep-1905004321 (staging-gpu-3) — collecting kernel traces, latency histograms, kv hits. ETA ~3h.

jin: Quick note: kernel selector currently prefers fused_attn for seq<=512, falls back to generic for larger sequences. For streaming with longer histories we see fallbacks that spike latency jitter when mbsize increases. Example config fragment:

```
kernel_map:
  fused_attn: seq<=512 && qparams.quantized==false
  generic_attn: else
```

That fallback path is expensive on tail.

sam: Also remember KV cache hit-rate amplifies streaming benefits — test cache rates 0%, 50%, 90%. Streaming relies on prefix reuse, bulk completions less so. Suggest command: 

`./run_sweep --modes=streaming,bulk --mbsizes=4,8,16 --cache_rates=0,50,90 --profile=kernel,latency,kvcache`

emily: Pasting a quick batch from an earlier mini-run (staging-gpu-3) — raw numbers to orient:

```
mode       | mb | cache | p50  | p95  | p99  | throughput tok/s | kv_hit
streaming  | 4  | 90%   | 22ms | 210ms| 640ms| 12k             | 0.90
streaming  | 8  | 90%   | 26ms | 320ms| 980ms| 18k             | 0.90
streaming  | 16 | 90%   | 40ms | 510ms| 1400ms| 28k            | 0.90
bulk       | 4  | 90%   | 18ms | 120ms| 240ms| 8k              | 0.90
bulk       | 8  | 90%   | 24ms | 170ms| 300ms| 14k             | 0.90
bulk       | 16 | 90%   | 36ms | 230ms| 410ms| 26k             | 0.90
```

emily: Key takeaway: streaming p99 balloons for mb>=8 even with high kv hit — suggests scheduling / kernel tipping point rather than pure cache effect. Kernel logs show many sessions hitting generic_attn around token 512 due to system+history length.

jin: Agreed. Two levers to try: 1) raise fused_attn threshold (e.g., prefer fused up to 768) and 2) add a sticky kernel binding per-session so we avoid frequent selector flips mid-session.

corey: From infra side: mbsize affects ordering and last-shard blocking — larger mbsizes increase waiting for slow tokens which hurts tail. For streaming, recommended defaults: mbsize=4-8 and use adaptive batching with latency targets. E.g., adaptive_mbsize(min=2,max=8, target_latency_ms=300).

alex: Good signals. Action: run one more sweep with: adaptive_mb (min=2,max=8), kernel_thresh=768, cache_rates=[50,90], collect p95,p99, kernel_switch_count, cuda_stream_queue_depth. Post json/profiles.

perf-bot: Job queued: sweeplist-1905004321-adaptive-2 (expected runtime ~3h).

maya: Kicking it off now on staging-gpu-5. Will attach perf traces (pprof + nvtx) to the job.

alex: If kernel_switch_count > 5/session we should consider session-sticky kernel binding (or a per-session hint) to reduce jitter. Also watch cuda driver queue fragmentation — that caused spikes previously.

emily: Anecdotal: enabling sticky binding reduced p99 by ~200ms in a small AB test (mb=8 streaming, long history).

sam: Also watch for CUDA stream contention when many tiny batches enter the driver at once — that shows up as 1-2ms spikes accumulating into p99. We might need a small coalescing window for submission.

corey: If adaptive_mb can't hit SLO while keeping throughput, fallback plan: allow model-variant fallback for streaming sessions (lower-capacity variant for long-history sessions) and fall back to cached completions where acceptable.

alex: 👍 thanks all. Reconvene when perf-bot posts results. If anyone sees a surprising kernel_switch_count or kv_hit < expected, ping me directly. :thumbsup:

(maya will post final logs here once done)
